paper_title: A microwave paraphoton and axion detection experiment with 300 dB electromagnetic shielding at 3 GHz
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing chi, dimensionless (as plotted Log10 chi)
notes: Microwave light-shining-through-wall experiment at CERN searching for paraphotons (hidden/dark photons) via photon-paraphoton kinetic mixing at 2.9565 GHz. Only a single representative exclusion point is quoted in text/Fig.2: chi = 7.6e-9 at m_gamma' = 1.1e-5 eV/c^2. The full exclusion is a curve but only this point is given numerically. Not a DM haloscope, so no local density assumed. This is an LSW result, not stellar/cosmological. Confidence level not explicitly stated; assumed 95%. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.72, 23)) | Vision: Paraphoton (hidden photon) LSW experiment; kinetic mixing chi vs hidden photon mass. Figure 2 shows a downward-pointing cyan triangle with apex at the labeled best limit m_gamma=1.1e-5 eV, chi=7.6e-9. Lower boundary is the V-shape: left arm follows chi ~ m^-2 (slope -2 on log-log) up to chi=1 near m=1e-9 eV; right arm is a steep near-vertical cutoff at the ~2.9565 GHz (1.2e-5 eV) resonance. Right-arm mass values are approximate due to the steep, nearly-vertical slope. Text also notes a prior Coulomb-law limit chi<3e-8. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.00 snapped to identity)
